robotics/

Systems that sense, decide, and move

A quadruped that has to map a building while walking through it, and an IoT stack that carries a sensor reading from bare microcontroller all the way to a dashboard.

2025 to 2026·Undergraduate thesis·two-person team·graded A−

AXION: autonomous indoor navigation for a quadruped robot

DeepRobotics Lite3 Pro LiDAR · ROS 2 Jazzy · Cartographer SLAM · A* + MPC

My role
Two-person thesis. I owned the autonomous navigation system end to end: system architecture, ROS 2 integration, LiDAR SLAM and indoor mapping, global path planning and obstacle avoidance, integration with the Lite3 Pro platform, and every navigation performance test in this table.
My teammate Jurdiel Lappu built the computer-vision and interaction side (YOLOv8-Pose human detection, gesture and speech). Supervised by Aditya Heru Prathama, Ph.D. and Erwin Anggadjaja, Ph.D. at Calvin Institute of Technology.
Problem
A robot meant to guide people around a campus building has no GPS and no prior map indoors. It has to build its own picture of the space, know where it is inside that picture, and reach a point set by a human without clipping a wall, a pillar, or a person on the way.
Approach
Mapping. 3D-LiDAR returns into Cartographer SLAM, which corrects global odometry drift through loop closure, then out to a 2D occupancy grid saved via map_server as .yaml/.pgm. Verified against laser-measured wall, desk, and door dimensions rather than by eye.
Localisation and planning. AMCL localises the robot against the saved map; Nav2 runs A* as the global planner over a Costmap 2D carrying inflation zones, so routes keep a safe clearance instead of hugging walls.
Local control. A Model Predictive Controller re-solves the local trajectory each cycle to brake or steer around obstacles that appear mid-run, then rejoins the global route.
Architecture. Modular ROS 2 nodes over DDS for low-latency transport, so a stall in perception cannot take navigation down. C++ for the performance-critical algorithms, Python for the decision layer; a Finite State Machine orchestrates idle → follow → search → stop.

Why A* missed its target, and what it actually shows. Every one of the ten runs reached the goal, and every route was verified to stay in free space and clear of static obstacles, so the planner was geometrically correct. It missed the 10-second target because the robot was capped at 0.25 m/s instead of the 0.5 to 1.0 m/s design speed: the navigation stack ran on an external laptop, which could not carry the real-time compute load at nominal speed. The bottleneck was the compute platform, not the algorithm.

End-to-end IoT products and system prototypes

ESP32 & Arduino firmware · Node-RED · InfluxDB · Grafana

Problem
An IoT prototype is only useful if the whole chain holds. A sensor reading has to survive the trip from silicon to a screen someone actually looks at, and most prototypes break somewhere in between.
Approach
Wrote the firmware on Arduino Uno and ESP32, interfaced the sensors, and handled the link out.
Routed telemetry through Node-RED into InfluxDB as a time series, then built Grafana dashboards on top for monitoring.
Repeated the loop across two courses, Smart IoT Product Design (A−) and Smart IoT System Design (A), treating each build as a product rather than a demo.
Result
Working prototypes with a live path from sensor to dashboard, backed by coursework in microcontrollers & sensors, IoT architecture, energy for IoT, and web programming for IoT.

mechanical/

Product design, modelled to build

Personal design work in Autodesk Inventor. These are the real assemblies: geometry, colours and part hierarchy decoded straight from the STEP files, then rendered here in the page. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, and pick any part from the list to find it in the model. I take on CAD and mechanical design work alongside the embedded side.

webgl · from .step
Parts
    drag to rotate · scroll to zoom · click a part to pin it …
    STRIDER · 1100 × 581 × 766 mm

    A 1.1-metre quadruped built around a plate-frame torso: longerons, side plates, front and rear bulkheads, a top deck and a skid plate, with the battery tray and compute plate carried inside and a payload rail on top. The electronics bay holds a battery pack with its BMS and power-distribution board, two motor controllers, a compute module, an IMU, a LiDAR in the head pod and five depth cameras covering front, rear, both flanks and below, plus an emergency stop and two fans. Each of the four legs runs on three of my own actuators: a Pivot S at hip abduction, and a Pivot L at both hip and knee flexion.

    PIVOT L · 138 × 89 × 133 mm

    The larger of the two joints the legs are built on, shown assembled, so pick a part from the list to find it inside. A frameless motor (stator, windings, rotor hub and magnets) drives a harmonic gear set: wave-generator plug and bearing, flexspline, circular spline. Output goes through a hollow shaft to a flange carried on a cross-roller bearing, with a magnetic encoder on the rear. The lip seal and shims are modelled too, which is the difference between a shape and a part someone can actually order.

    PIP · 46 × 28 × 72 mm

    A 72-millimetre desk robot. Split head shells around an OLED behind its own cover, an antenna, a neck joint, a two-piece torso with a chest badge, upper and lower arms on both sides, and two legs. The PCB, cell and battery door are modelled as well, so the internal volume is a real constraint rather than an assumption.

    BEACON · 33 × 34 × 126 mm

    A 126-millimetre torch around a single 18650 cell, sealed at three points: an O-ring under the bezel, one in the head joint, one at the tail. The optical path runs LED on a metal-core PCB, reflector, lens, bezel; the driver sits behind its own retaining ring; the tail carries a switch on a separate PCB under a rubber boot. Body, pocket clip and cell spring finish it.

    teaching/

    Coaching students to the national round

    The other half of my work. I sat the National Science Olympiad twice and medalled twice. Now I turn that syllabus into problem sets students can actually beat.

    2023 to present

    Olympiad Trainer at the Indonesian Geography Olympiad Alumni Team & partner academies

    • Train high-school students for city, provincial, and national olympiad rounds.
    • Author problem sets and field-practice materials from scratch, rather than reusing past papers.
    • Coach the supervising teachers too, so the programme keeps running after I leave.
    • Work with 20+ schools and academies across Jakarta, Bekasi, Depok, and Tangerang, plus online cohorts.
    Credentials I teach from

    • Gold Medal, National Science Olympiad (OSN), Social Sciences, Indonesia, 2018.
